the effects of salt on the development of hypertension.

the evidence for the effect of dietary salt on blood pressure in salt-sensitive teenagers is inconclusive.
a diet low in sodium is beneficial in reducing blood pressure in the general population and in those with high blood pressure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study suggest the presence of a salt-sensitive group of adolescents with a higher prevalence of obesity and a greater blood pressure response to salt restriction.
the blood pressure response to salt is determined by the balance between the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and the natriuretic peptides.
the blood pressure change with age was significantly different among the salt-sensitive (SS) teenagers and normal teenagers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salt sensitivity is a major risk factor for hypertension in adolescents.
salt sensitivity can be detected early in adolescence, even before hypertension is established.
the salt-sensitivity of teenagers is not the result of their diet, as it is in adults, and that it is not related to the level of blood pressure in childhood.
